taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 491, Lupinus sparsiflorus var. arizonicus: plants 1-2 dm. high; var. barbatulus taller and stouter, to about 4 dm. in the photos.

traits.height_max_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: rarely over 50 cm, in wet years.

traits.life_span.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 434), Lupinus sparsiflorus var. barbatulus: keyed among the annual lupines.

traits.woodiness.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 434), Lupinus sparsiflorus var. barbatulus: an annual herb, somewhat succulent.

traits.rosette.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 434), Lupinus sparsiflorus var. barbatulus: stems stout and fistulous, leafy throughout: no rosette.

traits.cauline_leaves.note: The stem leaves as large as the lowest ones, spread along the branching stems, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 336406908, 338966375, 339109267, 194391602, 160803294, 158331293, 148212311, 10412272): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 434), Lupinus: leaves alternate, digitately compound.

traits.leaf_division.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 434), Lupinus: leaves digitate, of 4 to 15 leaflets.

traits.division_pattern.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 434), Lupinus: leaves digitate (palmate).

traits.division_order.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 434), Lupinus: leaflets entire, the leaf divided once.

traits.leaflets.note: Six to ten leaflets to a leaf, within the genus's 4 to 15 (Kearney and Peebles 1942 p. 434), set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 336406908, 338966375, 339109267, 194391602, 160803294, 158331293, 148212311, 10412272): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.leaflet_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: leaflets 1.5 cm to 3.5 cm long, two to four times as long as wide.

traits.leaflet_width_m.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 434), Lupinus sparsiflorus var. barbatulus: leaflets broadly oblanceolate, 5 to 12 mm wide, rounded and mucronate at apex.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: the blade, without its petiole, is the palmate leaf's leaflets, 1.5 cm to 3.5 cm long (the estimate of 4 cm to 10 cm counted the petiole, which leaf_length_m leaves out).

traits.petiole_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: petioles 3 cm to 7 cm long.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 434), Lupinus sparsiflorus var. barbatulus: leaflets broadly oblanceolate.

traits.leaf_apex.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 434), Lupinus sparsiflorus var. barbatulus: leaflets rounded-mucronate at apex.

traits.leaf_margin.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: leaflets entire, as in the genus.

traits.inflorescence.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 434), Lupinus: flowers in terminal racemes.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: racemes 5 cm to 20 cm long.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 434), Lupinus sparsiflorus var. barbatulus: flowers not more than 10 mm long; Abrams (1944 p. 491): flowers 8-10 mm long.

traits.flower_colour.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 434), Lupinus sparsiflorus var. barbatulus: corolla pale purplish pink; sRGB by eye from the photos (lilac to pink-purple).

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 434), Lupinus: papilionaceous flowers.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 434), Lupinus: papilionaceous flowers.

traits.fruit_type.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 434), Lupinus: a legume.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: pods 1.2 cm to 1.8 cm long.

traits.flowering_months.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 437), Lupinus sparsiflorus var. barbatulus: 3,000 feet or lower, abundant in sandy washes and on plains, February to May.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: pods ripen in April and May, before the plant dies in the heat.

traits.elevation_max_m.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 437), Lupinus sparsiflorus var. barbatulus: 3,000 feet or lower: about 910 m.

traits.light.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 437), Lupinus sparsiflorus var. barbatulus: sandy washes and open plains.

traits.soil_texture.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 437), Lupinus sparsiflorus var. barbatulus: sandy washes.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a branched annual with stout hollow stems, bright green palmate leaves, and loose spikes of lilac-pink pea flowers. Colours set by eye were written as screen (sRGB) shades; they are read as the linear light a colour field holds, and bark and foliage follow the stated colour traits by rule (2026-10-19). The hand-set leaflet width (0.16) and whorled flowers (four to a node) were dropped 2026-10-19: Kearney and Peebles (1942 p. 435) give "leaflets broadly oblanceolate, 5 to 12 mm. wide" and "Flowers not verticillate", so the leaflets follow leaflet_width_m by rule and the flowers stand singly along the raceme.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for Arizona lupine from its sources and the photos the traits cite, on the template of large-leaved lupine (lupinus-polyphyllus); an annual, it flowers in its first year (adult_age 1); the rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.3 m tall at 1 years in the open, within its sources' range, as it grows on a Sonoran Desert bajada. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Saguaro desert scene (west bajada, Tucson Mountain District, 2026-10-19): sizes and forms from FEIS, Kearney and Peebles (1942) and Abrams, counts and colours from iNaturalist photos, drawing values from the library's rules for the form.
